entities.summary: Indian grammarian (c. 4th century BCE) whose Ashtadhyayi (Eight Chapters) is the most comprehensive and scientifically rigorous grammar ever produced for any language in the ancient world. Using approximately 4,000 algebraic-style rules (sutras), Panini described the entirety of Classical Sanskrit morphology and syntax with a precision and economy that modern linguists compare favorably to formal computer languages. His work anticipated concepts of formal language theory, context-free grammars, and the Backus-Naur Form by over 2,000 years. Noam Chomsky and other modern linguists acknowledge Panini's profound influence on the development of linguistic science.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Panini's Ashtadhyayi laid foundational principles for linguistic analysis and formal language theory, influencing Noam Chomsky's work on generative grammar by over 2,000 years. His comprehensive grammar of Classical Sanskrit remains the most scientifically rigorous in the ancient world.
